cli.services_heavy.heavy: Wait for, or run a command holding, the machine-wide heavy-job slot
cli.services_heavy.heavy_description: Heavy builds and test runs share a few slots per machine so that parallel builds cannot exhaust its memory. 'wait' blocks until a slot is free without taking it; 'run' takes a slot, runs one command while holding it and frees it when the command exits; 'status' lists who holds each slot. Use these instead of polling for another process by name.
cli.services_heavy.wait: Block until a heavy-job slot is free, without taking it
cli.services_heavy.run: Run one command while holding a heavy-job slot, and free the slot when it exits
cli.services_heavy.status: Show the heavy-job slots and each holder's pid, age and command
cli.services_heavy.timeout: Longest to queue for a slot, in seconds (default: the machine's queue limit, {wait_seconds}s unless {env_name} sets another)
cli.services_heavy.no_command: Nothing to run: put the command after `--`, for example `lop services heavy run -- make test`
cli.services_heavy.start_by: Latest time the command may start: epoch seconds or ISO-8601 with an offset or Z (e.g. 2026-11-19T08:05:00Z). Checked after the queue wait, just before the command starts; if it has passed, the command is not run and the exit status is 79
cli.services_heavy.late_start: late start: start-by {start_by} passed (now {now}, {late}s late); command not started
cli.services_heavy.not_start_by: {value} is not epoch seconds or an ISO-8601 time with an offset or Z
